title: EU AI Act Article 13: Transparency and Instructions for Use for High-Risk Providers
context: 2026-08-14 engine cycle -- EU AI Act high-risk obligations live (Aug 2, 2026); Article 13 transparency duty binding for providers of high-risk systems
body: EU AI Act Article 13 requires providers of high-risk AI systems to design and develop them so their operation is sufficiently transparent to enable deployers to interpret output and use it appropriately. The obligation is structural, not cosmetic: transparency here means the system must expose enough about its purpose, capabilities, limitations, and expected inputs and outputs that the provider can draft accurate instructions for use and the deployer can exercise meaningful human oversight. For a verification-first operator this is the entry point to a verified measurement credential -- a transparency claim that stays self-asserted is a marketing statement; a transparency claim backed by an independent, signed record of measured behaviour is evidence. The Council of AI reads Article 13 as a measurement obligation in disguise: you cannot honestly tell a deployer how a system behaves unless you have measured that behaviour, and you cannot make that measurement auditable unless it is signed and reproducible. The posture is monitored containment, not provable isolation -- Article 13 transparency does not prove the system is safe, it proves the boundary between what the provider claims and what the system measurably does is watched and verifiable. Concretely: (1) every high-risk surface must ship a machine-readable capability-and-limitation record. (2) That record must carry an independent signature so a downstream auditor can verify the transparency claims against measured behaviour rather than the provider's word. (3) The record feeds the Council of AI Containment Incident Index, so a divergence between claimed and measured behaviour is traceable to a boundary event.
references: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act), Article 13 -- transparency and provision of information to deployers
